etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle French invective, from Medieval Latin invectiva (“abusive speech”), from Latin invectīvus, from invectus, perfect passive participle of invehō (“bring in”), from in- + vehō (“carry”). See vehicle, and compare with inveigh.
senses: An expression which inveighs or rails against a person.
A severe or violent censure or reproach.
